parsed.explanation: No criminalisation or entry ban, but combined regime imposes biological-sex rules on facilities, policing, custody and health care. The equality code and top-court ruling allow single-sex exclusion; transport and one regional police search by sex at birth; prison placement follows birth sex; hospital ward plans and a documented cancer-ward death indicate severe care harm. Media/official threat-framing and falling acceptance signal hostile climate. Protections—gender-reassignment law, GRCs, courts and advocacy—are mostly resident-facing or unresolved for visitors, so they do not offset state-imposed searches/custody. Adult and travelling minor face facility, care and search exposure; no documented execution or identity imprisonment. Elevated Risk, near 0.45.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented entry denial, but presentation/document mismatch can trigger transport/security checks; no traveler-specific border friction recorded.
entry_documents.protection: No trans-specific immigration bar; home passport accepted under general entry; equality law still covers gender reassignment.
entry_documents.interaction: Matters only at airport/rail/security if stopped; not general visa/resident LGR.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Interim policy: trans women strip-searched by birth-sex officers; regional police search by biological sex; prison placement by sex at birth challenged but restrictive.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No identity crime; courts, ombuds and advocacy possible; lived-gender officer on request in one force.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If visitor is stopped, arrested or jailed, searches/custody become birth-sex.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Statutory code interprets sex as biological for single-sex spaces (changing rooms, hostels, services); some schools/sports excluded trans girls; one region diverging.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Gender-reassignment discrimination remains protected; legal challenge/UN criticism pending; operators vary.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Everyday accommodation/transport/venue use can expose mismatched marker.

care_services.exposure: Planned ban from opposite-sex hospital wards, intimate care by biological sex; documented death after cancer-ward removal; minors: no new puberty blockers/hormones.
care_services.protection: Gender reassignment care approved via NHS/private; emergency care general; no visitor-specific refusal recorded.
care_services.interaction: Illness/injury can force ward, searches, disclosure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Top-court, ministerial, police and prison policies frame biological sex as controlling for safety/privacy; anti-trans media vitriolic; official warnings ignored.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Functioning courts, GRC process, equality-body complaints and legal action exist.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile law plus efficient institutions creates traveler-facing exclusion.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor faces reduced youth gender-care, service closures, ward/intimate-care by birth sex, possible school/sport exclusion; guardian may need disclose.
minors_guardians.protection: Trans youth covered by equality act; private care possible; some regional protections.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult-minor care/facility encounters are birth-sex constrained.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented traveler attacks, but survey/Gendered Spaces fears harassment and hostile media raise risk of confrontation/ejection/service refusal; police can misgender/search.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Some regions hate-crime/speech protections; rule-of-law generally; no organized sweeps documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response varies by region and incident; complaints may expose.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Legal challenge to code/policy, prison challenge, inquest unresolved; no evidence remedies protect visitors promptly; hate-crime laws only some regions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts, ombuds, advocacy groups, anti-discrimination law and UN attention exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Formal remedies may delay/force disclosure without guaranteed outcome.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 exposure: routine institutional checks, humiliating searches and care denial. Here, however, no deceptive-presentation criminal statute and more formal protections; but prison/search/ward rules are documented, so score sits around this anchor.

Worse than 0.55-C: both have hospital/document mismatch harm, but this dossier adds statutory single-sex exclusion, birth-sex strip searches and birth-sex prison placement with documented fatal ward harm, while visitor remedies are unresolved.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor has trained border/marker matching, respectful searches and rapid remedies; here transport/regional police search by birth sex, facilities exclude, and no traveler-facing border protection is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines entry tolerance with hostile facility and policing rules. For an adult, the main exposure is not deportation but discovery in a checkpoint, service, hospital or police encounter: equality law interprets sex as biological, and interim search/custody policies place the person by sex at birth. This produces invasive intimate searches, exclusion from congruent facilities, and possible birth-sex prison or ward harm. For a minor, health-service restrictions and school/sport exclusions deepen discovery and care delays. Formal protections and courts are present, but they are mostly resident-facing, slow, or unresolved, and functioning institutions enforce the restrictive rules. Absence of criminalisation and execution keeps the score in Elevated Risk rather than High/Severe.
